Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with pain on urination (dysuria) for just under a week.
Chief_Complaint.source_text: I've uh it quite hurts when I kind of pee... it's been going on for about just under a week.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: The pain is a burning, stinging sensation.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I notice a sort of burning, stinging, when I when I go to the toilet, yeah.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports urinary frequency, which is impacting her ability to attend university.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: it's like I'm going to the toilet a lot more... I'm just like constantly looking for the toilet.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient has associated aching pain in the lower abdomen (suprapubic), which is worse on urination.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: it kind of hurts sometimes when I'm, like in at the bottom of my tummy as well... mainly when I go to the loo, I think that's when it's worse.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient noticed pink-colored urine with some frank blood today.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: today I noticed, um, that it was like a bit pink... of any kind of frank blood? I mean red blood at all, in your urine? Yeah, I think just today .

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient denies nausea, vomiting, or fever.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: No, no nausea vomiting... Any temperatures or fevers? Um no, no not that I've noticed.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports no new changes to her usual bowel habits related to IBS.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I don't think it's any, different, from what it usually is.

Past_Medical_History.content: Patient has a history of Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS).
Past_Medical_History.source_text: I think I have, um, IBS

Medications.content: Patient takes the combined oral contraceptive pill.
Medications.source_text: Uh yeah, uh I'm um on the pill... Uh, combined pill.
I take, um, something for the IBS as well. Um it begins with an M... Mebeverine? Yeah, yeah that's it.

Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.content: Patient is allergic to an antibiotic, possibly Clindamycin.
Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.source_text: Um, yeah I think there was an antibiotic, um, called Clindamycin

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is a 19-year-old university student studying English.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I'm Amanda Jackson and I'm nineteen years old... I'm studying, uh, English.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is in a long-term relationship and is sexually active; she does not use condoms but is on the contraceptive pill.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I have a, a long-term, um, boyfriend... I don't really use condoms with my boyfriend

Social_and_Family_History.content: Last menstrual period was two weeks ago.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: when was your last period? Um, two weeks ago.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient lives in university halls with a flatmate.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I am living in halls at the moment, uh at uni... I'm just living with a flatmate I suppose

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient does not smoke cigarettes but tried cannabis ('weed') for the first time a week and a half ago.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I don't smoke... I smoked weed for the first time... a week and a half ago

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient drinks alcohol occasionally and socially.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I drink occasionally, um, kind of socially, um, with friends .

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient has no relevant family history.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: in terms of family history, any history of problems with the bladder or the kidneys? No, no.

Assessment.content: The impression is a simple urinary tract infection (UTI) or cystitis.
Assessment.source_text: I think it's, um, probably just a simple what we'd say a UTI or a cystitis, bladder infection.

Plan_of_Care.content: Prescribed a 3-day course of antibiotics, either Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: so we've got a choice of two antibiotics something called Trimethoprim or, Nitrofurantoin which is a three day course.

Plan_of_Care.content: Arrange for the patient to provide a urine sample (MSU) for lab analysis.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: It's probably worth giving us a urine sample today as well if you can, so we can send it off to the lab.

Plan_of_Care.content: Advised to increase fluid intake and use simple analgesia like Paracetamol for pain.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: make sure you're well hydrated, drink plenty of fluids... if you are having some pain, simple Paracetamol, um, would probably be advisable.

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient to return for review next week if symptoms are not improving.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: but if things still are still not getting any better next week come back and see me, and we can have another look again.

Follow_up_Information.content: Advised on red flag symptoms for urgent review: fever, back pain, or vomiting.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: do bear in mind those symptoms I mentioned about the fever and the back pain and vomiting. If you have any of those give me a call, OK?
